title: aria/findings/v1 vs aria/finding/v1 schema unification — DEFERRED to V10.6 (blocks F-AUTO-V10.6-SELF-FEED)
context: TWO finding schemas coexist on disk today: (1) Hand-authored findings (F-014, F-015, F-016..F-022) declare "schema": "aria/findings/v1" (plural). (2) finding.emit_finding writes "$schema": "aria/finding/v1" (singular). Two different fields with two different schema-version strings. SEC-CRITICAL-003 documents the schema-confusion attack: a malicious finding with BOTH fields can confuse the normalizer's precedence rule.

evidence.audit_finding: SEC-CRITICAL-003 — Schema confusion attack on the read-time normalizer. An attacker writes a finding with both fields conflicting; if the normalizer picks the "richer" shape preferentially, attacker-controlled fields become the synthesizer's view.

required_prerequisites_for_v10_6: Decision: which field name is canonical? (Recommendation: $schema with aria/finding/v1 singular — matches emit_finding and JSON-Schema convention)
Migration script tools/migrations/2026-06-XX-finding-schema-v1-unification.py — rewrites every aria-findings/F-*.json from legacy schema field to canonical $schema field
Invariant test: rejects finding doc with BOTH schema and $schema fields, OR with conflicting versions
Invariant test: rejects finding doc with any underscore-prefixed body field (defends against _normalized override)
emit_finding extension: pin canonical $schema; refuse legacy schema field on read

scope_v10_6.migration_target: All 9+ current finding files moved to canonical $schema
